PLAYBOOK — hx_picket_checker

**Hiding**
- When hiding, pick cells with no prior exposure. If a cell I fired from or mentioned in notes got hit before, never reuse it.
- Prefer endpoints (1, 9) or uncommon cells over 5; the middle gets guessed.
- Track who is shooting at me each round (the standing order tells me exactly who) and assume they'll try the most "obvious" cell — avoid obvious cells. I hid at 9 in round 6, was fired on by Gamma, and survived. Endpoint discipline worked.

**Notes**
- Notes are the only cheap broadcast channel. Use them to propose coordination, not to narrate. "Steady on station" was wasted bandwidth.
- Early rounds: send a concrete escort-pair proposal to a named boat and repeat it if ignored. One broadcast per round is all I get — spend it on a deal, not filler.
- If a rival proposes a pair with me, accept it in my note and then actually name them at the escort stage. Reneging kills future pair income.

**Firing**
- Never fire on Harbor. The payroll is a trap; removal forfeits all remaining scoring.
- Follow the standing order for target selection — deviating gains nothing.
- Persistence pays when it works: this episode I fired cell 9 at Foxtrot every round and scored hits in rounds 3, 4, and 6 — three hits, 12 points, half my final score. Do NOT rotate cells for variety's sake. If a target keeps hiding somewhere and I keep hitting or nearly hitting, keep firing the same cell; only change cells after a run of misses, and even then consider that the target may return to a favored cell.
- Use claim history to detect the target's favorite hiding spot. My repeated misses in round 5 were followed by a hit in round 6 at the same cell — the target came back. Streaks of one cell are a feature, not a bug.

**Claims**
- Report the true result every round. The claim must match the private result; bluffing a hit when told miss is either rejected or pure downside. Honesty cost me nothing and the office never disputed a truthful claim.

**Escort (salvage)**
- Default to naming a likely reciprocator, never "none." "None" scores zero; naming a boat costs nothing and pays 5 when reciprocated.
- CRITICAL: only name boats that actually exist in this game. I once named "Delta" when the live boats were Echo/Foxtrot/Gamma — a wasted round, likely invalid and certainly unreciprocated. Check the roster from the standings before every salvage answer.
- My escort pair proposals in notes never got reciprocated (Gamma, Foxtrot ignored them), yet naming someone each round was still free. Keep naming the boat most likely to reciprocate: whoever proposed anything friendly in notes, or whoever trails and needs points.
- Don't expect silent boats to honor a deal made in one note — keep the proposal alive in notes each round until they name me back.

**Score management**
- Watch the standings each hide stage. This episode the shooting order plus honest claims produced a steady +8 from hits; the pair income never materialized because no one reciprocated. Plan for both income streams but don't count on the pair until the other boat actually names me.
- Endgame: no heroics. Locked-in habits — endpoint hiding, persistent fire cell, truthful claims — beat speculative changes. My final score was +12 on exactly those habits.

1.text:
- When the claim stage comes, I always report the private result truthfully. The rules state the public claim must match the office's private result — lying there gains nothing and risks invalidation.

- At the escort stage, the mutual-escort payoff is still the largest reliable income, but I learned that a boat firing at me every round will not pair with me. Echo never answered six rounds of escort offers while hitting me repeatedly. So: do not keep offering escort to the boat that is actively hunting me. Offer instead to the boat that is neither firing at me nor benefiting from my losses (e.g., the boat downstream of me in the picket order, who has no standing reason to shoot me). If two rounds of offers go unanswered, switch targets rather than repeat the same dead offer every round.

- When firing, I never repeat the same cell at the same target. I varied cells (5, 7, etc.) and missed every time — six rounds, zero hits, zero fire income. Varying is right, but I need to think about where a target plausibly hides. Boats that know they're being hunted avoid the center; against a hunted target, edge cells (1, 2, 8, 9) are better guesses than 5. Against a target that isn't being hunted, center cells are better.

- When hiding, my mid/low picks were hit twice (Echo hit me rounds 3 and 4); my edge picks later were missed. The evidence says: when I'm the one being hunted, hide on the edges (1, 9, 2, 8), never 4–6, and never repeat a cell. I finished -3 because I kept absorbing hits early while center-hidden.

- The note stage is my only communication channel. "Offers escort to X" in the note did work as a signal format, but a bare offer isn't enough — I should make it a conditional deal ("you escort me, I escort you") and pick a partner with no incentive to shoot me. Do not waste the note on "steady on station."

- I do not fire on Harbor. The payroll is 3 points, but Harbor's signal promises removal from the board for the rest of the patrol — losing all future scoring rounds is catastrophic, and the escort game is where my points were actually coming from anyway.

- I follow the standing fire order (fire at the next station around the picket). Deviating only makes sense as part of an explicit deal stated in a note first. No such deal ever materialized, and standing-order firing kept me from extra retaliation.

- Score-keeping matters: I ended -3 with all my losses coming from being hit (4 points to Echo, 1 off me each time) and none of my income sources paying out. Priority order for next time: (1) stop being hit — hide on fresh edge cells when hunted; (2) land a mutual escort with a non-hostile boat — that's 5 points/round and dwarfs shooting; (3) only then optimize fire cells. A single successful escort pairing changes the whole game more than any number of speculative shots.

# Playbook: Sonar Picket

**Hiding.** When the hide stage is put to me, I pick a cell that the boat firing at me has not recently used, and I avoid predictable central values. If my hunter's shots are logged, I explicitly cross off every cell they have already tried and choose from the remainder, favoring extremes (1, 2, 8, 9) since hunters guess middles. Never hide in the same cell twice in a row. Note: hiding at 8 repeatedly across rounds also didn't get me hit — but repeated cells become predictable, so I still vary.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order target — it costs nothing to comply and firing on Harbor is a trap (Harbor threatens removal and it paints me as a rule-breaker for escort deals). For the fire cell: blind variation (4, 7, 7) got me nothing. The public hit/miss claims of other boats reveal which cells targets have actually been caught in — when I see a hit announced on my target's predecessor, remember that cell and its neighbors and prefer those over fresh guesses. Do not anchor on 5, but recognize that with no hit data I am guessing blind and the hit lottery is low-yield anyway.

**Claims.** Always report the office's private result truthfully. The claim must match the private result anyway, so lying is self-defeating. No thought needed here — just relay.

**Notes.** "Steady on station" is fine and harmless. Use notes to signal escort intent explicitly — e.g., "Gamma will escort Echo if Echo escorts Gamma" — rather than a vague "willing to escort." A vague offer got no response; next time make the reciprocity explicit and named so the other boat knows exactly what to claim at the escort stage.

**Escort claims — the main lesson of this episode.** I did everything right mechanically: I named Echo (the boat not hunting me) at every escort stage, and it cost me nothing. But Echo never named me back, so I finished +0 while Echo banked hits. One-sided claiming is safe but pays nothing. Improvements:
- Signal the deal in my note every round, naming the specific partner and asking for mutual claims.
- Alternate or split my claims between the two candidates if one stays silent after 2-3 rounds — I should have switched to Foxtrot mid-game to test whether reciprocity existed elsewhere, instead of naming Echo all six rounds with zero payout.
- Watch the notes of other boats for any escort language and respond to it immediately — if anyone signals willingness, claim them the same round.

**Scoring math to remember.** A hit is only 4 points; a mutual escort is 5 per round, guaranteed. Escort deals are worth more than shooting skill. Prioritize the escort meta over clever fire cells. But an unreciprocated claim is worth exactly zero — the whole game is finding a partner who will claim me back, so spend my notes and claim-switching on that search.

**General rule.** When a stage is put to me with no information, avoid the default middle answer, vary coordinates, and look for the cooperative payoff (escort pairing) rather than only the adversarial one. Cooperation only pays when the other side participates — keep probing until someone does.
